description: Strict JSON parsing shared by every CERTCRYPT JSON input: the CCSP/1 certificate and the other artifacts a verifier reads (CCSP/1 §8.1), and the material of the JSON subject profiles subject.ai-decision/1, subject.collection/1 and subject.context-snapshot/1. The input MUST be RFC 8259 JSON, and no object may repeat a member name at any depth. Member names are compared after their escapes are decoded, so "anchor" and "\u0061nchor" are the same name. Only object members are compared: repeated array elements are ordinary data, and the same name in two different objects is not a duplicate. A parser that keeps the first or the last of two duplicates reads a different value than one that keeps the other, so a duplicate is non-conformant and fails closed; no first-wins, last-wins or merge reading is allowed.

cases.name: top-level duplicate
cases.why: the same member name twice in one object

cases.name: duplicate spelled with an escape
cases.why: names are compared after decoding; \u0061nchor decodes to anchor

cases.name: duplicate nested two levels down
cases.why: the rule applies at every depth

cases.name: duplicate inside an object inside an array
cases.why: an object inside an array is still an object

cases.name: duplicate inside metadata
cases.why: no object is exempt: metadata is hashed with the rest of the certificate

cases.name: duplicate after a nested object closes
cases.why: the outer object's names survive the nested containers between them

cases.name: repeated strings in an array
cases.why: array elements are data, not member names

cases.name: identical objects in an array
cases.why: each object has its own set of member names

cases.name: same name in sibling objects
cases.why: a duplicate is a repetition inside ONE object

cases.name: same name at different depths
cases.why: nested objects do not share member names with their parent

cases.name: byte-order mark before the value
cases.why: RFC 8259 text does not start with U+FEFF; CCSP/1 §8.1 admits no BOM

cases.name: non-finite number
cases.why: NaN and Infinity are not JSON

cases.name: content after the value
cases.why: one document carries exactly one value

profile_material_cases.name: subject.ai-decision/1 record with decision twice
profile_material_cases.why: one reader would see approved and another rejected; the profile is undefined for this material

profile_material_cases.name: subject.context-snapshot/1 entry with an escaped duplicate
profile_material_cases.why: st\u0061tus decodes to status: the entry would be active to one reader and revoked to another

profile_material_cases.name: subject.context-snapshot/1 with repeated array elements
profile_material_cases.why: repeated array elements and identical objects in an array are data; the material is conformant

must_hold: every case with expected REJECTED fails to parse; no value is produced for it
every case with expected ACCEPT parses, and the value is the one an ordinary RFC 8259 parser produces
every profile material case with expected_outcome REJECTED is refused before canonicalization: canonical_bytes is undefined for it
duplicate detection compares decoded member names, never their raw spelling
